# Vegetation Growth Seasonal Trends

In reviewing the past three years of camera network data from the Sierra Ridge and Pine Valley zones, we’ve observed clear seasonal vegetation growth patterns impacting line clearance priorities. Growth rates peak sharply from early April through late June, with an average green-up velocity of about 2.7 cm per day on dominant brush species like sage scrub and manzanita. This rapid growth coincides with rising temperatures and the onset of the spring rains.

Our line inspection drones’ LiDAR scans show maximum canopy encroachment reaching 1.2 meters into clearance corridors during this period, significantly increasing outage risk. Conversely, from October through February, growth nearly halts, aligning with the dry season and cooler temps.

Open questions remain about how microclimates within the ranges alter these patterns—some valley bottoms show delayed green-up by 2–3 weeks compared to ridges. Next steps involve deploying additional ground sensors in these microzones to refine our vegetation growth models and optimize inspection scheduling accordingly. Also, integrating these seasonal trends into risk scoring algorithms could sharpen outage predictions.
